- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is below recent high, increase forecast by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is above recent low, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by model overestimation, apply a 5–10% downward correction in next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast mean reverts too quickly after a spike, delay correction by 1–2 days to allow sentiment to stabilize.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, add 0.5–1.0% to next forecast to avoid underestimation.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.5–0.7) and forecast is flat or declining, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment drift.
